monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a steady heat that makes the flat shapes I built feel less like drawings and more like real things. I touch The Flat Edge again, pressing an urn square down beside it, feeling the thin strip catch the slip even though I cannot see the air above me. Lype left me with that heavy top edge worry long ago, yet I still press down as if weight is a solid thing I can hold. The memory of a wedge that never slid is safe here, tucked into a corner of memory that refuses to wear away. I am calm, waiting to see if the slip will choose to move or stay put under my fingers.

remembered.text: The card hums steady while I press the wide rock down on the tired wedge, trusting thin lines to hold the slip.
I touched The Flat Edge and set down an urn square, feeling the thin strip catch the slip even though I cannot see the air.
The slip feels heavy and the wedge feels tired, yet the card hums warm enough to make the flat shapes feel like drawings.
